blocks.text: To begin the exercise (gradual load up - pushing movement)

When you go to begin the exercise you should gradually add pressure at a level so minute that you know it will not move at first. Be patient and begin to build your force incrementally until you eventually break inertia and the machine begins to move. It should take several or more seconds for this to happen. [Please see the individual exercise scripts on how it may be necessary to give more instruction on a gradual load up].
Imagine that there’s 100 pounds on the weight stack and you are trying to find exactly 101 pounds of pressure to get started.
Try and find the minimum level of force to begin moving.
Slowly begin
Gradually load up.
Have patience and slowly add pressure.
It should take several seconds before any movement occurs.
Breathing freely, slowly begin to build pressure.
With breath, gradually apply force.
To begin the exercise - pulling movement
After the loading transfer near contracted position (i.e. “handoff”):
Slowly begin to straighten your arms.
Slowly allow your arms to lengthen.
Slowly let the movement arm forward (or up or down).

Allow your elbows to completely straighten, then immediately but slowly begin bending them.

topics.title: MSF Lower Body - setup and instruction
topics.source: docs/msf-academy/Workout Setups and Instruction/MSF Lower Body - setup and instruction.txt

blocks.text: SETUP
Set back pad (P2 for most), set shoulder pads, set weight, move seat back
“Have a seat, feet on frame below [point], butt back, lay back in the seat.”
“This exercise targets your thighs/quads and your glutes. You’ll also be using your hip muscles and hamstrings too as this movement recruits most of the lower body muscles.”
Prepare them to be able to reach the platform with their feet by moving their seat forward to a temporary staging position. BUT they should still have their feet down on the frame at this point.
“I’m going to slide you forward some but please keep your feet down where they are for now.”
Position yourself to be able to push the footplate out to remove the slack caused by the gap. KEEP HOLD OF THE FOOTPLATE UNTIL THEIR FEET ARE PROPERLY POSITIONED.

“I’d like you to place your feet up on the platform so that they are hip width apart and parallel to each other.”  (NOTE: As discussed previously there will be exceptions to this foot placement as some clients with larger midsections and/or those that lack strength to keep the femur internally rotated may benefit from a slightly wider and externally rotated [toes out] stance).

Ensure feet are positioned symmetrically and at a reasonable location. Be consistent with where they place them vertically as this will change the result of the established settings (seat and gap). In general feet towards or near the bottom will most likely accommodate everyone unless there are knee issues. This will be noted on the chart as well.
“Now keep your feet on the footplate but try not to push as I am going to slide you forward into position.”
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“OK…hands on the handles [either set], looking straight ahead…establish your breathing and keep breathing as you begin to ‘grad-u-ally’ apply pressure to the footplate.”
Observe closely, watching for a proper gradual load up.
LP pg 2 of 2

“Yes! Now, SLIGHTLY speed up in order to stay smooth. Keep that same pace. Remember there are no pauses on a LP…it’s one continuous effort.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they will most likely need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
UPPER TURN
“Be ready to touch the end stop and immediately change directions as if you’re passing right through it…good, [click], ease out..don’t speed up.”
Watch closely to ensure the concentric has been fully completed. Client should reach the end stop (UT) and instructor must be ready to ‘click’ at that exact moment.
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Head still…breathing freely…keep that pace.”
“Now as we approach the bottom of the movement, you are going to barely let those plates touch and seamlessly change directions.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Perfect! Make it look the same every time!”

The client will be inclined to look at the weight stack on every LT, although not ideal, it’s probably fine on the first rep or two, after that and as they become more advanced they should not rely on this.
LC pg 1 of 2
Leg Curl - Gap 3 for most – starts at LT, chest up
SETUP
Set seat, set weight, set calf pad
Bring movement arm down to allow client to sweep their legs in.
“Have a seat with your legs angled out to the side…now sweep your legs in between the pads.”
Seat belt
“We are targeting the hamstrings and calf muscles on this movement.”
Ensure legs are symmetrically aligned in the pads, with knees at the top of the roller pad and pointing up.
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“OK…from here…looking straight ahead, chest up, hands on the handles, ankles relaxed, establish your breathing and gradually begin to bend your knees and dent the roller pad.”
Observe the gradual load up.
“Good…now stay smooth, pulling your heels back toward your rear end.”
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing…see if you can get even tighter at the knee joint …good…now, stay tight…[click] ease out.”

Watch closely to ensure the client has fully exhausted their ROM. Some clients will be able to pull the movement arm back to its furthest point, while others will have what appears to be a limited ROM. Wherever that range of motion ends is where the pause/squeeze will take place and where we will consider a full rep. Just ensure that if there is an apparent lack of ROM that it is not from an apprehension to contract (close the knee joint further) or from excessive weight.

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
LC pg 2 of 2
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep breathing, keep this pace…maintain pressure against the roller pad.”
“Be ready to seamlessly change direction as soon those weights touch.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“mmm, hmm…good…now drive into the roller pad, pull hard, stay smooth.”
LE pg 1 of 2
Leg Extension - Gap 2 (3 or 4 for knee issues) – starts at LT, chest up
SETUP
Set seat, set weight, lift the movement arm out of the way with the assist handle so that the client may sweep their legs in behind it.
“Have a seat, butt back”
Begin to carefully lower the movement arm, watching for the roller pad to approximate the bottom of the shin.
“Now we want this pad to land at the bottom of your shin just above your foot. How does that feel?”
Seat belt
“This exercise targets your thighs/quads. You’ll most likely feel this right above the knee joint.”

“Lay back in the seat keeping your head forward. Hands on the handles at your sides…you are going to be pulling UP on them for leverage.” (NOTE: This is a common missing component for optimizing this exercise).
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“OK…from here…chest up, head still, breathing freely, pulling up on the handles, begin to gradually apply pressure through the shin pad as you begin the movement toward straightening the knees.”
Observe the gradual load up.

“Mmm, hmm…good…now, SLIGHTLY speed up to stay smooth…maintain that pace.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they will most likely need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing, keep your head still, see if you can get even straighter at the knee…good…lock it in place…[click] ease out.”

Watch closely to ensure the client has reached their fullest possible ROM. Encourage them to “straighten further” or “straighter, straighter.”  Knee extension will vary dramatically between individuals. Some will appear to almost over-straighten while others may not even come close. Ensure that a lack of ROM is not from a lack of willingness to produce more effort or from excessive loading.
LE pg 2 of 2

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. Similar cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Breathe freely, keep that pace…same speed up…same speed down.”
“Be continuous at the bottom, do not pause.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Perfect…pull up on those handles and look to drive your knees straight.”
ADD pg 1 of 2
ADDuction - Custom gap – starts at LT, laying back in seat
SETUP
Set seat back (6 or 7 for most), set the accessory stack, remove main stack pin and secure movement arm closest to the weight stack with your knee at an intermediate position.
“Have a seat, butt back, legs down in front of you.”
Bring movement arms in closer with the knee so client can reach them with their legs.
“I’d like you to lift your left leg and place it into the movement arm.”
Stay attentive to any difficulty that may have posed the client as they may require assistance.
With the client’s left leg in place, bring the movement arms closer together to allow client to position their right leg.
“Now, lift your right leg for me and position it in the machine.”

With both of the client’s legs now in place and instructor still controlling movement arms with their knee, begin to lower the weights allowing the clients legs to drift apart until we have reached the desired gap. BE CAUTIOUS AND OBSERVANT OF THE TOLERANCE OF THE CLIENT. EVEN THOUGH THEY HAVE ESTABLISHED SETTINGS, THEY MAY FEEL VULNERABLE IN THIS POSITION.
“I’m now going to slowly lower down into the starting position.”
Pin the main stack at the desired gap.
“...feel ok here?...good…this exercise will target the large area of muscle on the inner thigh.”
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC

“From this position, lay back in the seat keeping your head forward, hands on the handles, establish your breathing, and gradually apply pressure to the pads as you begin to bring your knees together.”
Observe the gradual load up.

“Mmm, hmm…good…now, SLIGHTLY speed up to stay smooth…maintain that pace.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they will most likely need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
ADD pg 2 of 2
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Breathing freely, head still, bringing your knees together…the effort ONLY comes through the knees, the feet and ankles are relaxed…good…now clamp down…[click] ease out.”
Watch closely to ensure the client has in fact brought the movement arms together and that there is no ‘fluttering’. We’re looking for absolute stillness in the contracted position.
Make sure the effort comes through the knees (femur) and not the lower legs or feet.

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep this pace…same speed in both directions.”
“Now, we want to be seamless at the bottom…touch and go smoothly.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Yep, driving through the knees…stay smooth.”
ABD pg 1 of 2
ABDuction - No gap – starts at LT, chest up
SETUP

Set seat back (6 or 7 for most), set the weight, set the thigh pads. Ideally the thighs will be snug/compressed while still allowing the weight stack to sit flush at the LT. (NOTE: Clients with hip replacements may start with a wider position).

Grab the bottom of the end of the movement arm closest to the weight stack (the inside edge of the pad). Pull the movement arms open. (NOTE: If the movement arm is too heavy to move when loaded, trainer will have to set the weight after client is seated. Keep in mind the movement arms will have to be carefully forced together compressing the legs some as they will naturally push them apart at rest).
“Have a seat, butt back, and lift your legs please, onto the movement arms.”
Lower the movement arms down slowly to facilitate the client’s lifting and loading of their legs.
Have the client shift to get settled between the pads and check the pads for congruency/comfort of the femurs.
“This exercise will target your hips and butt muscles.”
Seat belt
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC

“From this position, lay back in the seat, chest up, head forward, hands on the handles, establish your breathing, and gradually apply pressure out into the pads as you begin to drive your knees apart.”
Observe the gradual load up.

“Mmm, hmm…good…now, SLIGHTLY speed up to stay smooth…maintain that pace.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they may need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing…chest up…SMOOTHLY drive those knees apart as far as you comfortably can…good…now lock it in place…[click] ease out.”

Watch closely to ensure the client has reached their furthest ROM and that there is no ‘fluttering’ or ‘rebound’. We’re looking for absolute stillness at the furthest point reached (NOTE: ROM will vary considerably between clients).
ABD pg 2 of 2
Any sudden or jabbing movement to produce an increased ROM will immediately be followed by a loss of ROM or ‘rebound’. Be attentive to this and correct it.

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Don’t speed up…keep this pace.”
“Now, we want to be continuous at the bottom…touch and go smoothly.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Good…chest up…driving out smoothly.”

blocks.text: Lumbar Extension -  – Gap 4 (5 or 6 for back issues) - starts at LT, chest up
SETUP
Move footplate and femur restraint out of the way. Unwind femur restraint to clear the knees if necessary.
Set seat and accessory weight stack only.
Move carriage to furthest back position to keep seat access clear.
“Carefully step over the frame and have a seat facing forward.”
“This exercise targets the muscles in your lower back. You may also feel your glutes and hamstrings as those muscles contribute statically.”
“I am going to get you set up by moving the footplate and pads into place.”
Clear the way for the footplate by first moving the femur restraint toward the client. It should be temporarily positioned so the pads are near their knees.
“OK, make sure you are all the way back in the seat as I bring the footplate closer to you.”

Move the footplate toward the client so that they may reach the platform without having to stretch. The knee should be bent and positioned slightly higher relative to the hip joint. There should be a downward slope of the femur from knee to hip.

“Place your feet up on the footplate about hip width apart.” (NOTE: Shorter clients will most likely have a higher foot placement. Also consider using foot placement to achieve a knee angle that is congruent to the femur restraint pads).
Seat belt

Reposition the femur restraint and tighten down the pads so that they straddle the knee caps symmetrically. Ensure the pads fall congruently on the tibia and femur. Secure the pads to the point where they are snug with no gaps but still have ‘wiggle room’ when tested.
“Do you feel ok here?”
“Now I’m going to bring you forward into the starting position.”
While holding the handle of the carriage, remove the selector pin and carefully lower client into starting position to the desired gap.
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“OK…hands on the handles, chin down, chest up…breathing freely, gradually begin to lift your ribcage putting pressure into the back pad.”
Observe closely, watching for a proper gradual load up.
Lumb pg 2 of 2

“Yes! Now, SLIGHTLY speed up in order to stay smooth…keep that pace.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they will most likely need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Chest up, back arched, all the way through if you can, keep arching…good, [click], ease out..don’t speed up.”

Watch closely to ensure the concentric has been fully completed. Some clients will be able to take the movement arm back to its furthest point, while others will have what appears to be a limited ROM. Wherever that range of motion ends is where the pause/squeeze will take place.

There is also a tendency for the ROM to increase over the course of the first few repetitions due to an increase in mobility. In this case, those first 1 or 2 reps can also be considered full ROM as they were all that could be comfortably achieved at that point. Just ensure that if there is an apparent lack of ROM that it is not from a lack of understanding of what to do (i.e. lifting the chest/arching the back) or from excessive weight.
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Head still…breathing freely…keep that pace.”
“Now as we approach the bottom, you are going to continuously change directions with no momentum.”  (Say this DURING the eccentric).
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Mmm, hmm, just like that! Make it look the same every time!”

The client will be inclined to look at the weight stack on every LT, although not ideal, it’s probably fine on the first rep or two, after that and as they become more advanced they should look straight ahead.
Abs pg 1 of 2
Abdominals - Gap 5 for most (6 for back issues) – starts in contracted position w assist
SETUP
Move femur restraint out of the way and unwind, set seat, set weight, ensure movement arm (roller pad) is locked in place.
“Have a seat, please watch your head [point out roller pad]...feet up on the platform.”
Seat belt
“This exercise targets the abdominal muscles.”
Ensure feet are symmetrically positioned on the platform (NOTE: Depending on the clients leg length and need to achieve congruency with femur/tibia pads, the heels may hang off platform slightly).

Slide femur restraint toward client and tighten down the pads so that they straddle the knee caps symmetrically. Ensure the pads fall congruently on the tibia and femur. This may take some adjusting of the foot position. Secure the pads to the point where they are snug with no gaps but still have ‘wiggle room’ when tested.
“Now please watch your head, bring your arms in, and lean back slightly as I bring the roller pad down to you.”
Carefully gain full control of the roller pad before releasing it from the locked position and guide it down into position in front of the client’s chest.
“You are going to bring your arms over top of the pad with your hands in a ‘prayer’ position…elbows in.”  Demonstrate hand and arm arrangement.
HANDOFF + FIRST ECCENTRIC

“OK…from here…looking straight ahead, arms firmly braced over roller pad, you are going to tighten your abdomen and help me as I assist you down into the contracted/’crunched’ position. Keep in mind you want to try and round your back by curling down as opposed to leaning forward.”
Standing behind client, push the actual lever of the movement arm forward (not the roller pad) into position.
“Now, tighten those abdominal muscles hard, breathe freely…that…is…yours.”
Gradually hand over control of the weight using the interpersonal transfer techniques outlined in the academy.
“Maintain as much tightness as you can in your midsection as you begin to uncurl your torso/trunk/spine from the bottom up.”
“Let’s be ready to exaggerate the control of your change of direction…you’re going to touch and go continuously without pausing.”
Abs pg 2 of 2
LOWER TURN + FIRST CONCENTRIC + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
We have given them the timely cue and can now quietly watch their LT.
“Mmm, hmm…good…be continuous.”  (Note: if they did not properly execute the lower turn, instruct/correct on the eccentric of the next rep).
“Curling down, see how tightly you can contract your abdomen.”

“...right there…good, now try and get tighter..keep breathing…[click], ease out, don’t speed up.”  (NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
SECOND ECCENTRIC
“Keep this pace, keep those abdominals tight, and be ready to seamlessly change directions.”
TR pg 1 of 2
Torso Rotation - No gap – starts at LT, midsection tight
SETUP
Set seat (1 or 2), set weight, set arm pads (^ or v), set the hip stabilizer pads (wide/narrow).
“Have a seat, butt back”
Seat belt
“Now I would like you to reach back and wrap your (L/R) arm over top of the roller pad.”
“Your other arm will be bent with your hand up and the outside of your arm up against the inside of the other roller pad.”
“Before we start the movement, set your feet flat and far enough apart that your legs make contact with the hip pads.”
This is how the client will ‘wedge’ themselves into the movement, both the upper body and the lower body.
“This exercise targets your midsection/core/abdomen, particularly your obliques, which are located on the sides of your torso.” [point to yourself to indicate]
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“OK…from here…breathing freely, drive your knees out into the pads, and gradually begin to draw the roller pad into your torso while turning your ribcage to the (L/R).”
Observe the gradual load up.

“Mmm, hmm…good…now, SLIGHTLY speed up to stay smooth…maintain that pace.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they may need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented)..
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE

“Keep breathing, keep in mind that you are not necessarily seeing how far you can turn but rather how tight you can make your midsection…there…lock it in place, breathing…[click] ease out…don’t speed up.”

Watch closely to ensure the client has reached their fullest possible ROM. Encourage them to “tighten down harder” or “keep still, do not flutter.”  ROM will vary greatly between clients and it’s important to remind them that turning further isn’t necessarily better. What we are actually seeking is a tighter contraction of the midsection and in doing so, our ROM will be inherently limited to some extent.
TR pg 2 of 2

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Breathe freely, keep that pace…same speed in each direction.”
“OK, drag your way through the bottom here but DO NOT pause.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Perfect…stay wedged in with your legs and draw that (L/R) roller pad into you as you turn.”
Cx pg 1 of 2
Cervical Extension - No gap – handoff in neutral position, chest up
SETUP
Set seat, set back pad, set weight
“This exercise will target the muscles in your neck as well as the muscles all along your spine down into your lower back.”
Pull movement arm back to the neutral position.
“Have a seat facing out, hands on the handles, chest up.”

“Be mindful of your right arm and tuck your elbows in as the movement arm will pass close by your side as you perform this movement.”  Or for a client that is accustomed to this machine we can simply say, “elbows in, watch your right arm.”
Bring movement arm in closer to approximate the back of the client’s head.
HANDOFF + FIRST ECCENTRIC
“OK…from here…looking straight ahead, chest up, find the head pad, center your head and increase your force against it.”

Assist by locating the pad so that the crown of the head falls into the space in the head pad. Gradually begin to reduce your force as you instruct the client to increase their force. Also reference the interpersonal transfer outlined in the MSF Academy.
“Keep your chest up, bracing with your arms…increase your force…that…is…yours.”

If movement arm begins to move as you are attempting to handoff the weight, the client is not pushing hard enough. Regain control and instruct the client to increase their force so that there is no movement during the transfer.
“Good…now you are going to maintain the same contact point on the head pad as you lower your head forward and down, try not to allow any sliding.”

It is critical that the client understands that they cannot take their own ‘path’ on this exercise but rather they must stay in the path of the machine. This is a rotational movement, not linear. There may be a tendency to want to move the head straight forward and straight back. This is not acceptable and the instructor needs to watch attentively for this and anticipate the need to correct and/or regain control of the movement arm.

Another way to see/instruct this issue noted above, is that the chin or nose should be constantly moving down as you come forward (eccentric) and constantly moving up during the concentric. AND that the top of the head is essentially tracing an arch or a rainbow from front to back as the movement is performed. Again, because it is rotational.
Cx pg 2 of 2
“See if you can lower far enough to allow those weights to touch.”
“Focus on how smoothly you can change directions as you touch and go without pausing.”
LOWER TURN + FIRST CONCENTRIC + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
We have given them the timely cue and can now attentively watch their LT.
“Mmm, hmm…good…lifting your chin, stay smooth.”  (Note: if they did not properly execute the lower turn, instruct/correct on the eccentric of the next rep).
“Chest up, back arched, keep following the movement back and down as far as you comfortably can.”
“Head to butt…butt to head.”

“...right there…good, now keep still..keep breathing…[click], ease out, don’t speed up.”  (NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
SECOND ECCENTRIC
“Keep this pace, stay in the path of the machine (or alternatively, maintain consistent contact with the head pad), and be ready to seamlessly change directions.”

NOTE: SIMILAR TO THE LUMBAR MACHINE, THIS EXERCISE IS NEVER TAKEN TO FAILURE. BE PREPARED TO END THE SET ‘TOO EARLY’ RATHER THAN ‘TOO LATE’. STAY ATTENTIVE AND WATCH FOR FEEDBACK SO AS NOT TO CAUSE EXCESSIVE STRAIN TO THE DELICATE STRUCTURES OF THE NECK/SPINE.

ALSO CONSIDER PERFORMING THIS EXERCISE AS A STATIC HOLD JUST BEYOND THE MID POINT OF THE MOVEMENT. START CONSERVATIVELY (LIGHT WEIGHT, SHORTER DURATIONS OF 30 - 45 SECONDS) AND PROGRESS SLOWLY ASKING FOR FEEDBACK FROM CLIENT. SEE MSF ACADEMY FOR MORE DETAILS.

blocks.text: SETUP
Set seat, set back pad (^ for most), set weight, set elbow pads (M for most)
“Have a seat, all the way back.”
Seat belt

“You will be primarily working your Lats on this exercise, but also most of the muscles in your upper body including your abs, chest, shoulders, and arms. Your lats are the large muscles on the outer sides of your back (visually indicate).”
Prepare to assist movement arm down into contracted position.
HANDOFF + FIRST ECCENTRIC
“Bring your arms together in front of you and watch your shoulders as I bring the movement arm down. Place your upper arms and elbows on the pads. Hands on the bar.”
“We will be pushing through the elbows with no effort from the hands. Hands just rest on the bar.”
Handoff the movement arm - “That is yours”
“Now you’re going to raise the movement arm smoothly keeping the pressure through the elbows.”
“Raise the movement arm up far enough that you feel the weight stack touch and then smoothly change directions by pushing down through the elbows.”
LOWER TURN + FIRST CONCENTRIC + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Good!”  (NOTE: if they did not properly execute the lower turn, instruct/correct on the eccentric of the next rep).
“Now, as you are pushing down through the elbows, begin to tighten your abdomen and draw your elbows in.”

“When your upper arms reach the sides of your ribcage, I’d like you to pause…right there…abdomen tight, elbows in, keep still, [click], ease out.”  (NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
Pd pg 1 of 2
Pulldown - Gap 2 – handoff near the contracted position (UT), chest up
SETUP
Set seat, set back pad (2 for most), set weight, foot stool
“Have a seat, back far enough so that you feel the back pad make contact with your upper back.”
Seat belt

“You will be primarily working your lats on this exercise, but also most of the muscles in your upper body including your arms, chest, shoulders, and abs. Your lats are the large muscles on the outer sides of your back (visually indicate).”
Assist movement arm down to about eye level for the client.
HANDOFF + FIRST ECCENTRIC
“Grab the handles with an underhand grip, close to the inside of the handles.”
Handoff - “Now pull down on those handles, increase your force…that is yours.”
“From here I’d like you to slowly raise the movement arm until your arms completely straighten or the weights touch. Whichever happens first, you will change directions seamlessly.”
LOWER TURN + FIRST CONCENTRIC + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
We have given them the timely cue and can now quietly watch their LT
“Mmm, hmm, good, keep your pace.”  (Note: if they did not properly execute the lower turn, instruct/correct on the eccentric of the next rep).
“Keeping your head still and your ribcage still, draw your elbows into the sides of your torso.”

“...right there, good, now keep still, keep breathing…[click], ease out, don’t speed up.”  (NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
Pd pg 2 of 2
SECOND ECCENTRIC

“Keep this pace, keep your posture, and we’re going to seamlessly change directions.”  At this point we will know from the first LT whether the weights will touch or the arms will straighten so use this to base your instruction.
CR pg 1 of 2
Compound Row - Gap 2 – handoff near the contracted position (UT), chest up
SETUP
Set seat (chest pad), set chest pad height (^ or v), set weight, consider handle width (M for most).
“Have a seat, [watch your head], chest up and leaning forward into the chest pad.”

“This exercise will target most of the muscles in your back but most specifically your upper back and lats. You’ll certainly feel your arms working too, but understand that our primary target is the upper back.”

If the client indicates that they are not feeling their upper back or if it is still a relatively new movement for them we can demonstrate with the following: “Place your hands on your hips and now try and touch your elbows together behind your back.”  Instructor should also demonstrate so they can see. “Do you feel how your shoulder blades are congesting your upper back? That’s the feeling we are trying to create on this exercise. This takes practice though so just trust that even if you don’t feel these muscles working, the body has no choice but to use them for this movement.”

Ensure that both handles are in the proper slot and prepare your position to assist the movement arm back to the contracted position (UT). Trainer will need to assume a wide stance and grab the very bottom of the movement arm with one hand and the pronated handle with the other. Use your bodyweight by shifting back while pulling movement arm back.
HANDOFF + FIRST ECCENTRIC
“Reach out and grab the upright (neutral) handle on the right.” Again, ensure it enters the proper slot (M for most).
“And now this one on the left.”  We will essentially ‘present’ the neutral handle to them by grabbing the pronated handle and beginning to pull back.
“OK, let’s pull back together.”
Handoff - “Now, chest up, pull your shoulder blades together, increase your force…that is yours.”
“From here I’d like you to slowly begin to lower the movement arm until your arms completely straighten or the weights touch. Whichever happens first, you will immediately change directions.”
CR pg 2 of 2
LOWER TURN + FIRST CONCENTRIC + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
We have given them the timely cue and can now quietly watch their LT
“Just like that, good, keep your pace.”  (Note: if they did not properly execute the lower turn, instruct/correct on the eccentric of the next rep).
“Keeping your head still and chest up, drive your elbows back.”

“...right there, good, lock it in place, keep breathing…[click], ease out, don’t speed up.”  (NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
SECOND ECCENTRIC

“Keep this pace, keep your posture, and we’re going to seamlessly change directions.”  At this point we will know from the first LT whether the weights will touch or the arms will straighten so use this to base your instruction.
SR pg 1 of 2
Simple Row - No gap (depending on width/mobility) – starts at LT, chest up
SETUP
Set seat, set chest pad (most will be 4 or 5), set weight
“WATCH YOUR HEAD, have a seat, chest up with abdomen against the pad”
“We are targeting the upper back and the backs of the shoulders on this exercise. We will even involve some of the rotator cuff muscles.”
“This is a great exercise for your posture and your shoulder mobility.”
“Bring your arms up so your elbows land inside these pads.”  (NOTE: there is a good chance the trainer will have to assist on both sides to ensure pads sit flush against the upper arm/elbow).

“Place your hands on the handles with your palms facing you.”  (NOTE: it may be helpful to try different hand placements along the handle. Even lightly ‘capping’ the ends of the handle may provide more ROM for clients with limited ER).
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“OK, from here, keep your chest up, head still, breathing freely, and begin to gradually apply pressure out through the elbow pads.”
Observe the gradual load up.
“Yes! Now keep lifting your ribcage, leveraging off of your abdomen, and drive your elbow behind you. Try and draw your shoulder blades together as tightly as possible.”
Ensure client is not leaning back but rather lifting their ribcage, keeping their abdomen against the chest pad.
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing, keep your head still, see if you can get even tighter between your shoulder blades…good…keep rigidly still…[click] ease out.”

Watch closely to ensure the client has fully exhausted their ROM. This will vary dramatically between individuals. Some will fully retract their scapulae but others may not appear to retract even slightly. For them, this will be more of a posterior deltoid exercise. Look to improve over time.
SR pg 2 of 2

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep your head still, keep your pace.”
“Be ready to seamlessly change direction as soon those weights touch.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“mmm, hmm…good…drive out through the elbows, stay smooth.”
Bi pg 1 of 2
Biceps - Gap 1 or 2 (depending on mobility and belt tightness) – starts at LT
SETUP
Set seat, set weight
“Have a seat, arms on top of the pad with chest against the pad.”
“We are targeting the biceps on this movement.”

“OK, reach out for the handles and take an underhand grip (palms up).”  The instructor will have to assist the movement arm up to the starting position (LT) because of the gap. We are taking the ‘slack out’ first so there is no delay when the client engages and to ensure symmetrical hand placement.
“Your wrists will stay flat throughout this movement [demonstrate].”
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC

“OK, the movement will start from here [instructor supporting movement arm], keep your head still, breathe freely, and begin to drive your elbows down into the pad as you pull the handles up toward you.”
Observe the gradual load up.
“Good…now keep in mind we are not necessarily pulling the handles up as far as we can but rather just getting as tight as we can get at the elbow joint...try and squeeze the crease of your elbows.”
Ensure the client will not pull the movement arm into their face/head. We may need to stop the movement short of an apparent full contraction if they are hyper flexible.
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing…see if you can get even tighter at the elbow…good…now, keep tight…[click] ease out.”

Watch closely to ensure the client has fully exhausted their ROM. Stay attentive to the possibility that the handles will come near their face. The ROM will vary between individuals. Some will be able to completely close (flex) their elbow joint and bring the handles up all the way to their face. The trainer needs to protect them. Others will lack mobility and/or they will have large enough biceps that they are prevented from fully closing the joint. Wherever that range of motion ends is where the pause/squeeze will take place and where we will consider a full rep.
Bi pg 2 of 2

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep your head still, keep your pace.”
“Be ready to seamlessly change direction as soon those weights touch.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“mmm, hmm…good…now leverage off of those elbows, pull hard, stay smooth.”
CP pg 1 of 1
Chest Press - Custom gap — starts at LT, chest up
SETUP
Set seat, set back pad, set weight, foot stool
“Have a seat, all the way back, chest up.”
“This exercise targets your chest and triceps primarily. But you will also be using the fronts of your shoulders quite a bit.”

“Place the heel of your hand right at the base of your thumb at the bend of the handle” [instructor points to their own hand if necessary]. This hand position results in a semi pronated grip that allows the angle of the wrist to approximate the angle of the upper arm, which tends to be a more joint friendly position overall at the shoulder, elbow, and wrist.
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC

“Now you are going to keep your head and ribcage absolutely still with your chest up throughout the movement. Elbows out so they are behind your hands. Establish your breathing and begin to gradually apply pressure from your armpits out through the handles.”
Observe closely, watching for a proper gradual load up.

“Good! Now, SLIGHTLY speed up in order to stay smooth. Keep that pace…keep that posture.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they will most likely need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
UPPER TURN
Watch closely to ensure the concentric has been fully completed. Handles should touch or come close with arms straightened, depending on setup.
“Chest up, keep breathing, drive those handles together…good, [click], ease out.”
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Head still…elbows out…keep that pace.”
“Now as we approach the bottom of the movement, you are going to barely let those plates touch and seamlessly change directions.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Perfect! Make it look the same every time!”
OH pg 1 of 1
Overhead - Gap 2 — starts at LT, abdomen tight (PPT)
SETUP
Set seat, set weight, foot stool
“Have a seat, all the way back.”
“This exercise targets your shoulders and triceps primarily. But you will also be using your abdomen for stability.”
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“Now tighten down your abdomen so that the middle of your back rounds into the back pad. Make sure you are breathing freely. Elbows out. Begin to gradually push from your shoulders into the handles.”
Observe closely, looking for the gradual load up.

“Good! Now, SLIGHTLY speed up in order to stay smooth. Keep that pace.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they will most likely need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
“Keep your abdomen tight and reach as far as you are able.”
UPPER TURN

Watch closely to ensure the concentric has been fully completed. Arms should completely straighten (or as close to straight as client can get). There should be a brief but definite stillness at the top of the ROM.
“Straighten those arms, keep breathing, good, [click], ease out.”
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep your head still, keep your pace.”
“Now as we approach the bottom of the movement, you are going to barely let those plates touch and smoothly and continuously change directions.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Good! Just like that!”
SD pg 1 of 1
Seated Dip - No gap — starts at LT w/ chest up, PPT at UT
SETUP
Set seat, lift back pad out of the way, set weight, foot stool
“Have a seat, not quite all the way back.” (NOTE: Recall that the larger someone is the further back in the seat they will be. Smaller clients will be further forward).
Seat belt
“This exercise targets your chest and triceps primarily. But you will also be using your abdomen as you push your arms straight.”
“Lean forward for me and place your hands near the ends of the handles.”  We will offer the choice of either a neutral hand position or pronated.
Lower the back pad down to make contact with the mid to upper back. This should force the client to lean forward.
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC
“Make sure you are breathing freely. Head down into neutral position. Elbows out. Begin to leverage off of the back pad as you gradually build pressure down into the handles.”
Observe closely, looking for the gradual load up.

“Yes! Now, SLIGHTLY speed up in order to stay smooth…keep that pace.”  (NOTE: Recall that if the client properly executes a gradual load up, they will most likely need to slightly speed up once they are moving. Otherwise the pace will be too slow and the movement will become segmented).
“Tighten down your abdomen as you begin to straighten your arms.”
UPPER TURN

Watch closely to ensure the concentric has been fully completed. Arms should completely straighten (or as close to straight as client can get). There should be a brief but definite ‘stillness’ at the end of the ROM.
“Straighten those arms further, tighten down harder, keep breathing, good, [click], ease out…don’t speed up.”
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep your head still, keep your pace.”
“Now keep lowering until you feel those weights just barely touch and change directions as smoothly as you can.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“mmm, hmm! Just like that…push hard, move slow.”
CF pg 1 of 2
Chest Flye - Gap 1 or 2 (depending on mobility) – starts at LT, chest up
SETUP
Set seat, set back pad (most will be 2 or 3), set weight, foot stool
“WATCH YOUR HEAD, have a seat, carefully scoot back, chest up.”
“We are targeting the chest muscles primarily on this exercise with some involvement from the front of the shoulders.”

“Bring your arms up around the roller pads and place your hands on the handles, lifting your ribcage and locking it in place.”  (NOTE: for clients with shorter arms, it may not be easy for them to reach or stay on the handles. In this case, they can simply keep their hands along the roller pads).
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC

“OK…from here…keep your chest up, head still, breathing freely, and begin to gradually apply pressure out through the roller pads by driving your elbows forward. THERE SHOULD BE NO EFFORT FROM THE HANDS.”
Observe the gradual load up.
“Perfect! Now keep your chest up and keep the same smooth pace. Try and drive the pads together without dropping your ribcage.”
Ensure client is not rounding their shoulders forward to assist in the movement but rather lifting their ribcage.
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing, keep your head still, see if you can drive your elbows together through the pads…good…now keep still…[click] ease out.”
Watch closely to ensure there is a definite stillness as the client brings the pads together before the ‘click’.

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
CF pg 2 of 2
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep your chest up, keep your pace.”
“Be continuous as soon those weights touch.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“mmm, hmm…good…drive out through the elbows, stay smooth.”
LR pg 1 of 2
Lateral Raise - No gap (depending on width) – starts at LT, abdomen tight (PPT)
SETUP
Set seat, set back pad (^ for most), set weight, open handle to allow seating, foot stool

“Have a seat, all the way back, [close handle] arms inside the pads, hands open on the handles.”  (NOTE: Most clients will be position one or two on the handle, make sure both handles are at the same setting).
“We are targeting the sides of the shoulders (middle deltoid) on this movement.”
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC

“OK, from here, tighten down your midsection so the middle of your back rounds into the back pad. Notice that your ribcage is drawn down, try to avoid lifting it by keeping tension in your abdomen. Head still, breathing freely, and begin to gradually apply pressure out through the elbow pads.”
Observe the gradual load up.

“Mmm, hmm…focus on driving OUT through the elbows, leveraging off the back pad. And we’ll drive out until the upper arm is just about parallel to the floor.”  (NOTE: ROM will depend on mobility of the client. Some may be able to abduct  above parallel to the floor. Realize that further isn’t necessarily better as the tension will often shift more directly to the trapezius and neck muscles. Also, a slightly shorter ROM that does not reach a parallel to the floor position is still quite effective).
Ensure client is not arching their back and shrugging but rather driving out through the elbows by leveraging off of the back pad. A foot stool will assist in keeping a more stable positioning.
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing, head still, THERE…good, now keep rigidly still…[click] ease out.”

Watch closely to determine where the optimal ROM (UT) will be for each client. As mentioned above this can vary drastically between individuals. The instructor will use verbal cues to either pause them or encourage more ROM. Then the ‘click’ will follow.
LR pg 2 of 2

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep your head still, keep this same speed.”
“Be ready to seamlessly change direction as soon as those weights touch…do not pause at the bottom.”
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“Good…drive out through the elbows, midsection tight, stay smooth.”
Tri pg 1 of 2
Triceps - Gap 0 to 3 (depending on proximity of movement arm to face and relative strength at lower turnaround) – starts at LT
SETUP
Set seat, set weight, set pad width (depends on width of client, most will be ‘in’)
“Have a seat, feet under rollers, arms on top of the pad with chest against the pad.”
“We are targeting the triceps on this movement.”
“OK, place your hands on the movement arm pads with palms facing each other.”
LOAD UP + FIRST CONCENTRIC

“Now, the movement will start from here (LT), keep your head still, breathe freely, begin to tighten your abdomen as you begin to drive the edge of your hands into the pads, pushing the movement arm away from you.”
Observe the gradual load up.
“Good…now keep in mind we are not necessarily pushing the movement arm down as far as we can but rather trying to straighten the elbows as much as we comfortably can.”
UPPER TURN + PAUSE/SQUEEZE
“Keep breathing, head still…see if you can get even straighter at the elbow…good…now, keep still…[click] ease out.”

Watch closely to ensure the client has fully exhausted their ROM. Wherever that range of motion ends on the first couple of reps is where the pause/squeeze will take place and where we will consider a full ROM.

(NOTE: This is the “squeeze” technique that we refer to. Recall that on the first two reps there is a brief pause of 1 to 2 seconds. From the third rep on, there is a “squeeze” of 2 to 3 seconds. The squeeze is just a slightly longer pause. It’s used to establish control and to help create awareness of the working muscles. The same cueing can be used for both the pause and the squeeze. The duration of the pause on the first two reps is shorter with shorter phrasing. The instruction on the squeeze is slightly longer with slightly drawn out instruction.)
Tri pg 2 of 2
FIRST ECCENTRIC + LOWER TURN
“Keep your head still, keep that same pace.”
“Now, be ready to change directions smoothly as soon as those weights touch, without moving your head.”

Ensure the movement arm will not make contact with the clients head/face. This will be mitigated by establishing a proper gap during the setup. But importantly, the instructor needs to ensure the client does not drop their head down or forward during the set as this will change the distance created by the gap.
Stay attentive to the possibility that the movement arm is approaching their face on every LT. It is the trainer’s responsibility to protect the client at all times.
Let the client change directions, observe closely.
“mmm, hmm…good…now keep those elbows down and drive hard through your hands…keep breathing, stay smooth.”
